maria-cs: putting this here — FinePrint.ai (enterprise) reports cross-session prompt leakage when they use session pins. Customer provided repro steps and says this is happening intermittently, 2–3% of requests. They’re asking for a fix and a timeline.

maria-cs: repro steps from customer (copied):
```
# curl to reproduce
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/chat \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-live-fineprint' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"session_id":"fp-test-01","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Summarize: Q1 report"}]}'
```

maria-cs: expected: summary of Q1 report for session fp-test-01
maria-cs: observed (snippet):
```
{"id":"resp-xyz","choices":[{"message":{"role":"assistant","content":"Summary of Q4 marketing plan..."}}]}
```

maria-cs: they say the assistant returned content from a different session (fp-customer-archived).

liam-eng: thanks — assigning to eng-runtime. Can you paste a couple of request_ids and the approximate times? I'll try to repro in staging.

maria-cs: request ids: rid-a1b2c3 (2026-03-14T11:03:05Z), rid-a1b2c4 (2026-03-14T11:03:07Z). Customer also sent a tiny trace (attached to the support ticket).

liam-eng: reproduced locally in staging with a script that runs ~1000 sessions, saw ~0.8% cross-session hits. Looks like KV cache key derivation drops the owner namespace for session IDs with hyphens when under load. Quick dump: cache key = f"model:{model_id}:session:{session_id[:8]}" — using slice for speed introduced collisions across similar prefixes.

devin-ml: that slicing was a perf micro-optimization from the batching refactor. Under high QPS it reduces key length to speed hashing — but it can cause prefix collisions. We should consider namespacing and full-length keys.

liam-eng: proposal: P0 hotfix — revert prefix-slicing behavior and invalidate affected prefix-range in cache for customers with reported incidents. That should eliminate leakage with minimal risk. P1 longer-term — full session namespacing + test coverage + benchmark to measure perf delta.

ashley-pm: customer is enterprise with a committed Dedicated contract. This is a data isolation concern => high severity for them. We need a timeline and communication. Is hotfix deployable this week without breaking throughput SLAs?

liam-eng: I can do a hotfix branch: restore full session_id in cache key, add a short migration to drop prefix-index entries. Risk: small perf hit, maybe 3–5% tail latency increase on heavy workloads. We can gate on Dedicated customers by config flag.

devin-ml: alternative low-risk fix: add deterministic hash namespace (eg sha1(session_id)) instead of storing slices. That keeps key length stable while avoiding collisions. Probably safer than rolling back. Will add benchmark.

ashley-pm: prioritization decision: ship hotfix (sha1-namespace) as P0 targeting patch release this Friday EOD. P1: follow-up to add e2e tests, monitoring, and opt-in telemetry for session collisions, to be scoped into the next sprint. Need eng estimate for Friday.

liam-eng: estimate for hotfix (sha1-namespace + migration script + canary + rollback): ~2 devs * 2 days + 1 day oncall/testing. Can do it if we freeze minor perf changes for Dedicated customers behind flag.

maria-cs: I'll notify the customer with the proposed timeline (hotfix this week, follow-up tests next sprint). Also asked if they want us to pause batching for their tenant as a temporary mitigation — they said yes if it reduces risk.

ashley-pm: scope negotiation note: disabling intelligent batching for one tenant reduces throughput but lowers surface area. If customer prefers, we can offer that as an interim mitigation. Add to ticket.

liam-eng: creating eng ticket RDW-6124 with acceptance criteria: reproduce with unit test, implement sha1-based key namespacing, migration script to invalidate affected prefix keys, canary to 10% of Dedicated traffic, monitor for cross-session leakage < 0.01%.

devin-ml: I'll own benchmark and add microbench numbers to the ticket.

maria-cs: thanks — I'll update support ticket and schedule a 1:1 with FinePrint to share plan.

sre-bot: deploy window requested: 2026-03-19T22:00:00Z - 2026-03-19T23:30:00Z (canary first 30m)

ashley-pm: follow-ups: (1) PM note to backlog + mark as customer-driven urgent; (2) legal to confirm contract remediation language if needed; (3) postmortem checklist if broader impact.

maria-cs: noted. tagging eng-runtime and product for visibility. :white_check_mark:

liam-eng: will post progress updates in this thread.

maria-cs: closing loop here for now — thanks everyone. :heart:
